findings.review_scope: Registered-source content review of arXiv:2111.02826v4, stamped 1 October 2023, by Nilanjana Laha, Aaron Sonabend-W, Rajarshi Mukherjee and Tianxi Cai. This 50-page PDF is the main paper: discussion and acknowledgments end on page 42, a notice on physical page 43 links to a separate supplement, and references and main-paper figures continue to Figure 5 on page 50. The separate supplement was not opened. Fresh text evidence covers every main-paper page; source passages and theorem formulas were inspected as rendered images.
findings.inventory: Exactly seven actual bold Theorem headings occur: 1 (page 12), 2 (15), 3 (18), 4 (23), 5 (26), 6 (26), 7 (27). Theorem 4 continues with its complete type-B statement on page 24. All complete original statements, hypotheses, formulas, cases and probability qualifiers were compared against the PDF. Other result labels and ordinary-font citations are excluded.
original_statements: Theorem 1 preserves closedness, strict concavity, boundedness above, second-order smoothness, mixed-derivative regularity and the negative Fisher-consistency conclusion. The preceding source strict-concavity formula omits distinctness of x and y; that source defect is preserved separately.

Theorem 2 preserves the exact hinge function, Assumptions I-IV, positive lower outcome bound and both stage branches. Its capital H_1 in the failure clause, reordered history tuple, set-valued rules and scalar equality to a rule remain as printed.
Theorem 3 retains positive outcomes, I-IV, the product surrogate, Condition 2 and the exact divisor (C_phi/2)^2 in the regret inequality. No derivative-tail condition is imported.

Theorem 4 retains I-IV/A/B, the scaled approximation condition, the extra {0,1} domain factor, both type-A cases, alpha-prime restrictions and denominators, and the full type-B logarithmic/minimum/exponential bound on page 24.

Theorem 5 retains every rho_n and A_n condition, the scaled approximation with a_n=n^a and a>1, I-IV/A/B, all rate factors and the optimization-error maximum. It does not expressly assume either derivative type; this limitation remains documented.

Theorem 6 retains (23), rho_n in (0,1), A_n>1, its growth limit, the approximation rate, positive integer k, Opt_n<1/2 and I-IV/A/C. Theorem 7 instead bounds the bracketing count over U_n directly, uses its own approximation and growth conditions, says n>N_0 and retains no Opt_n<1/2 restriction. Both complete probability statements are preserved.
source_passages: All 30 source entries and 14 auxiliary passages were reviewed. The observed two-stage record, binary action coding, histories, empirical law, propensities, causal assumptions and integrability conditions match pages 5-7. Conditional reward contrasts and the continuation reward are separated from the assumption that their expectations are finite.

Optimal regimes, real measurable score pairs, original and surrogate values, potentially extended-valued maximizing scores, induced rules, regrets, eta ratios and sequential Fisher consistency match pages 7-9. The explicit no-attainment statement in Definition 1 remains recorded. The reward-ratio maps are not renamed treatment probabilities.

Closedness means upper semicontinuity here. Strict concavity retains the literal all-x,y quantifier. The hinge passage and strict reward comparison (13) remain distinct from the later product family. Condition 2 has strict increase, positivity, reflected-sum symmetry and limits without an added differentiability requirement.

The later product convention, empirical value, nested and product search classes, empirical optimization gap, known propensities and fresh-record population evaluation match pages 20-25. No exact empirical maximizer or named optimizer is assumed.

A is the printed upper outcome bound; B is the two-stage small-noise condition excluding boundary atoms; C literally says eta is bounded away from zero. Type A and type B preserve their different derivative bounds and kappa ranges. No source condition is silently repaired.

The source calls the bracket count entropy. Equation (21) bounds the count in sup norm separately for the two stage classes; (23) bounds log count in empirical L2 separately for them; (24) bounds the count in empirical L2 for the pair class. The exact norms, powers, class indices and unresolved quantifiers are retained.
findings.dependency_review: 61 direct uses and 126 deduplicated related connections were checked, including every direct list and all 30 related-theorem sets. Fisher consistency, closedness and strict concavity reach only Theorem 1; the hinge condition/function reach only Theorem 2. Condition 2 reaches Theorems 3-7. Derivative types reach only Theorem 4; small noise reaches 4/5; literal strong separation reaches 6/7. Empirical optimization and bracketing requirements reach only 5-7, with the specific sup-norm condition (21) only in 5. Proof-only neural-network, wavelet and extra smoothness assumptions are not imported.
findings.names_and_highlights: All 30 entries have source natural-language keywords and selectors matched to their original source labels/formulas or related same-paper theorems. Adjacent naming contexts and source types were checked. Assumptions I-IV/A/B/C remain assumptions, Condition 2 remains a condition, and numbered Definitions 1/2 retain their source identities. Symbol correspondence was inspected in addition to string occurrence.
findings.source_limitations: The 24 existing source notes were checked against the main paper. They preserve realized-action positivity, counterfactual scope, conditional versions, outcome shifts, history ordering, treatment coding and ties, zero-score behavior, maximizer existence, the strict-concavity diagonal, hinge shifts, Condition 2 smoothness, small-noise radius scope and contrast equivalence, strong-separation center, the later value display, approximation scaling, Theorem 5 derivative-tail scope and entropy/probability quantifier omissions. Source review establishes faithful extraction, not correctness of the printed results.
findings.changes: No census-content correction was required. The per-paper rebuild now uses the fixed verified source, and the finalizer docstring correctly refers to seven theorems. The earlier scripts are archived; the original audit and all six extracted JSON artifacts are preserved.
findings.validation: Separate inventory and census validators pass. All six regenerated artifacts match saved bytes. Registered-source identity, exact heading enumeration, continuation locations, graph sets, selector occurrence and artifact hashes supplement the completed manual source review.
